text:
1
+
+
+Has the wave no form?
+
+In one instant it sculpts itself
+
+and in another crumbles
+
+into the one that rises, round.
+
+Its movement is its form.
+
+
+2
+
+
+The waves withdraw
+
+—haunches, backs, napes—
+
+but the waves return
+
+—breasts, mouths, foam—.
+
+
+3
+
+
+The sea is dying of thirst.
+
+It writhes, with no one,
+
+in its bed of rocks.
+
+It dies of thirst for air.

translation.title: Facing the Sea
translation.editorial_note: The damaged source delimiters around the bodily lists are restored as dashes; wave-form becomes anatomy, then the sea’s impossible thirst for its elemental other.
